public.title: Nearest Hiding Ancestor
public.description: nodes is a parent-index tree in parent-before-child order; each node is {id,parent,hidden}, root parent -1. Return ID of the nearest node, starting at target and walking toward root, whose hidden flag is true. Return null if none. This adapter models supplied hidden flags, not CSS layout. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: The target itself can be the nearest hiding element.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and reference code, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party prose or code copied.

explanation: Check each node while following parent links and return the first hidden node. O(height) time and O(1) auxiliary space. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
